{
  "reviewer_task_id": "review-synthesis-web",
  "target_artifact": "/home/grammy-jiang/Projects/msgloom/research/04-reference-and-response-scope/runs/f72f7f513e9d/analysis/synthesis.json",
  "status": "accepted_with_issues",
  "issues": [
    "Contradiction 'One-to-one alignment assumptions versus empirically non-bijective reply structure' incorrectly groups manual-5a32708675 with one-to-one alignment assumptions. The NTCIR-16 overview explicitly represents potentially multi-sentence question and answer groups and expands each group into a full cross-product of sentence-level links. Its limitation is loss of finer proposition-level scope, not a one-to-one correspondence assumption.",
    "Contradiction 'Single-gold antecedent evaluation versus documented ambiguity and overlap' overstates what the supplied analysis of doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 establishes. That analysis reports one primary annotator per newly annotated document and shared-task gold evaluation, but it does not establish that each discourse-deictic case is evaluated against exactly one uniquely acceptable antecedent. The ambiguity-versus-exact-gold tension is directly supported by doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035, manual-be69c3aa17, and manual-7743c50805 without relying on this stronger characterization of the CODI-CRAC paper.",
    "The theme on cross-domain robustness cites doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 for the claim that methods specialized to one corpus or discourse convention can degrade under transfer. The supplied CODI-CRAC analysis establishes genre-dependent difficulty and an out-of-domain-training setup, but not a controlled in-domain-versus-transfer degradation result. doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999 directly supports the degradation claim, so the theme remains supportable but the CODI citation should be narrowed or its wording softened.",
    "Finding 'Several interrogatives in one turn cannot automatically be interpreted as several independent outstanding obligations' is faithful to doi-10-1016-j-pragma-2007-07-011, but its HIGH confidence rests on one abstract-only qualitative study in oral proficiency interviews. The finding is supported, but the synthesis should distinguish confidence in the observed phenomenon from confidence in transfer to workplace communication."
  ],
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "manual-5a32708675 is presented within a contradiction about one-to-one alignment assumptions even though its gold representation explicitly permits grouped multi-sentence question and answer material and evaluates their cross-product links.",
    "doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 is characterized as evidence for 'single-gold antecedent evaluation' more strongly than the supplied per-paper analysis supports.",
    "doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 does not, from the supplied analysis alone, directly demonstrate degradation caused by transferring a corpus-specialized method, although it does demonstrate genre variation and an out-of-domain-training setting."
  ],
  "required_fixes": [
    "Revise the first contradiction so manual-5a32708675 is described as a grouped/cross-product benchmark that loses proposition-level correspondence, not as evidence of a one-to-one alignment assumption. It may be retained as a related representational limitation but should be separated from the one-to-one side represented by doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999.",
    "Revise the third contradiction to avoid asserting that doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 uses a uniquely acceptable single antecedent unless that fact is established elsewhere. The methodological tension can be stated using doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035, manual-be69c3aa17, and manual-7743c50805, which directly document multiple acceptable, overlapping, or alternative antecedents.",
    "Narrow the cross-domain-robustness theme so doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999 supports observed transfer degradation, while doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1 supports genre dependence and the difficulty of out-of-domain evaluation rather than a measured transfer penalty.",
    "Consider lowering the transfer-level confidence of the multiple-interrogative finding or explicitly state that the observed evidence comes from oral proficiency interviews and does not establish workplace-message obligation structure."
  ],
  "confidence": 0.97,
  "scores": {
    "faithfulness": 0.94,
    "coherence": 0.91,
    "gap_completeness": 0.98,
    "citation_integrity": true
  },
  "notes": "The synthesis is broadly faithful and substantially stronger than the minimum needed for report generation. Its central conclusions are supported: zero-link and non-bijective structures occur; email and dialogue alignment cannot be reduced to adjacency; abstract antecedents can be clausal, discourse-segmental, discontinuous, overlapping, or multi-unit; proposition-level partial-answer and workplace approval/rejection/commitment scope remain unvalidated; and all five stated gaps are correctly left open. Transfer-domain evidence is generally labeled as such, and msgloom-specific abstention, proposition-state, and error-cost policies are explicitly framed as engineering hypotheses rather than empirical findings. All cited paper_ids belong to the permitted set. The remaining problems are localized mainly to how two contradiction entries characterize particular benchmark assumptions and to one secondary cross-domain citation; they do not overturn the executive summary or gap status."
}
